userInput.context:
The learner's own material, page by page:
[p1] BIOLOGIA - 1º ANO B - Prof.ª Juliana
Resumo pra prova de sexta (9/10): A CÉLULA
1) Teoria celular: todo ser vivo é formado por células (exceto vírus); a célula é a menor unidade da vida; toda célula vem de outra célula (Virchow); Hooke viu as "celas" na cortiça (1665).
2) Procarionte x eucarionte: procarionte sem núcleo (DNA solto = nucleoide), sem organelas membranosas, ex. bactérias; eucarionte com núcleo (carioteca) e organelas, ex. animais, plantas, fungos, protozoários; as duas têm membrana plasmática, citoplasma, ribossomos e DNA.
3) Membrana plasmática: bicamada de fosfolipídios + proteínas (mosaico fluido); permeabilidade seletiva; transporte passivo sem ATP (difusão simples, difusão facilitada, osmose); osmose: água vai do meio hipotônico para o hipertônico; hemácia em água pura incha e estoura (hemólise), em solução muito salgada murcha; transporte ativo gasta ATP, contra o gradiente (bomba de sódio e potássio); endocitose (fagocitose e pinocitose) e exocitose.
4) Organelas (CAI MUITO!!): mitocôndria (respiração celular, ATP); cloroplasto (fotossíntese, plantas e algas); ribossomos (síntese de proteínas); RE rugoso (proteínas) e RE liso (lipídios, desintoxicação); complexo golgiense (modifica, empacota e secreta); lisossomo (digestão intracelular); vacúolo (grande na célula vegetal); parede celular (celulose).
5) Núcleo: carioteca com poros; cromatina = DNA + proteínas; nucléolo produz ribossomos.
6) Vírus: acelulares, parasitas intracelulares obrigatórios; capsídeo de proteína + DNA ou RNA; antibiótico não funciona contra vírus.
A prof disse: vai ter questão de completar a tabela das organelas e uma dissertativa sobre osmose!

steps.conclusion: The required course boundary is violated: practical skills such as composing frames and manually balancing shutter speed and ISO are assigned to Photography rather than iPhone 13. Other Photography entries are conceptual rather than tasks performed on the phone. Two descriptions also need factual correction: the dual-crosshair level is for overhead alignment, not leveling horizons, and camera-to-subject distance determines perspective; changing focal length alone changes framing, not perspective.

Several skills bundle distinct actions, particularly shooting Slo-mo with Time-lapse and copying edits with exporting files. The video-editing skill includes Slo-mo adjustments but does not list the Slo-mo capture skill as a prerequisite. 'Hold the iPhone steady and prep lenses' is also product-specific rather than generically reusable.

Move focus and exposure practice ahead of the settings and format lessons to strengthen the early practical payoff. For third-party RAW capture, identify a compatible app and teach when its additional control is worth losing the convenience of the native computational-photo workflow.

steps.conclusion: The map violates the explicit course-placement requirement: practical camera skills such as framing subjects and changing camera distance are assigned to Photography rather than iPhone 13. Other Photography entries are framed as general conceptual analysis instead of tasks performed on the phone. These should become practical iPhone 13 skills, not a separate photography track.

Most phase titles describe activities or subject matter rather than stages of progress. Editing exposure and color unnecessarily requires Photographic Styles, although those capture-time styles are not needed to use Photos adjustments. Several skills combine separable actions, especially editing Portrait blur with copying adjustments, and organizing a library with exporting compatible formats.

Make the opening explicitly produce a better photo within the first few lessons. The current sequence starts with five settings lessons and four launch/shutter lessons before focus and exposure. A short shoot–inspect–adjust exercise would provide a clearer early payoff. Preserve the useful emphasis on judging light, distortion, sharpness, and editing results.
